---
{"publish":true,"title":"Convolutional Neural Networks","tags":["neural_networks","artificial_intelligence","CS2109S"],"PassFrontmatter":true}
---

A convolutional neural network takes a $n$-dimensional input.

# 2D input

Given a 2D input $X$, a sliding window is multiplied by the kernel $W$, to get the feature map.

Without any hidden pixels, and stride = $1$, if $X$ is $r_{x} \times c_{x}$ and $W$ is $r_{w} \times c_{w}$, the feature map would be of size $(r_{x}-r_{w} + 1) \times (c_{x} - c_{w} + 1)$.
